__broaden__.maxuma: maximus (maxumus), -a, -um — greatest, most important (n. acc./nom. pl.: maxuma, the greatest things) · also f. nom. sg. (maxuma Iūnō) · also f. voc. sg.
__broaden__.iuno: Iūnō, Iūnōnis (f.) — Juno, queen of the gods (nom. sg.) · also voc. sg.
__broaden__.remo: Remus, -ī (m.) — Remus, twin brother of Romulus (abl. sg.) · also rēmus, -ī (m.) — oar (abl. sg.)
__broaden__.placidaeque: placidus, -a, -um — calm, peaceful, gentle (f. dat. sg., with mortī) + -que, and · also f. gen. sg. + -que
__broaden__.videns: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see (pres. part., f. nom. sg.; vātēs videns) · also m. nom. sg.

culta: cultum, -ī (n.) — tilled land, cultivated field (usually pl. culta, -ōrum; n. acc. pl.)

flexus: flexus, -ūs (m.) — bend, turn, winding (of a river) (acc. pl.)

labris: labrum, -ī (n.) — lip; rim, edge of a vessel (abl. pl.; aquae … labris aēnīs, in bronze basins)
lacuaria: lacūnar, -āris (n.) — panelled ceiling, fretted roof (pl. lacūnāria; acc. pl., scanned lacuāria)
laomedontius: Laomedontius, -a, -um — of Laomedon, Trojan (m. nom. sg.; Aeneas as Trojan heir)
latina: Latīnus, -a, -um — Latin, of the Latins (f. abl. sg., with gente)
laurentes: Laurēns, -entis — of Laurentum, Laurentine (f. nom. pl., with nymphae)
laurenti: Laurēns, -entis — of Laurentum, Laurentine (f. abl. sg., ab arce; n. abl. sg., solō Laurentī; -ī for -e)
mactat: mactō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to sacrifice, slay as a victim, honour with offering (3rd sg. pres.)
manifestius: manifestus, -a, -um — plain, clear, evident (comp. adv. manifestius, more plainly)
minis: minae, -ārum (f. pl.) — threats, menaces (abl. pl.; terrēre minīs, to frighten with threats)

multasque: multus, -a, -um — much, many (f. acc. pl., with gentīs) + -que 'and'
pallante: Pallās, -antis (m.) — Pallas, Evander's forefather, Arcadian (abl. sg.; a Pallante, descended from Pallas)

pinguia: pinguis, -e — fat, rich, fertile (n. acc. pl., with culta)
populeas: populeus, -a, -um — of poplar, poplar- (f. acc. pl., with frondēs)
posci: poscō, -ere, poposcī — to demand, call for, claim (pres. pass. inf.; rēgem sē dīcere poscī, that he is called on)
procubuit: prōcumbō, -ere, -cubuī, -cubitum — to lie down, sink down, stretch out (3rd sg. perf.)
putes: putō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to think, suppose, imagine (2nd sg. pres. subj., in a nē-clause)
radiantis: radiāns, -antis — beaming, shining (pres. part. of radiō; f. gen. sg., with lūnae)
redeuntibus: redeō, -īre, -iī, -itum — to go back, return, come round (pres. part., m./n. abl. pl.; annīs redeuntibus)
refluens: refluō, -ere — to flow back, ebb (pres. part., f. nom. sg., with unda)
remigioque: rēmigium, -iī (n.) — rowing, oarage, crew of oars (abl./dat. sg.) + -que 'and'

ripa: rīpa, -ae (f.) — bank, shore (abl. sg.; also nom. sg.)

seramque: sērus, -a, -um — late, tardy (f. acc. sg., sēra quiēs, late rest) + -que 'and'
sicut: sīcut (adv., conj.) — just as, as, like
sistit: sistō, -ere, stitī, statum — to set, place, make stand; stand (3rd sg. pres.)
spectans: spectō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to look at, watch, gaze upon (pres. part., m. nom. sg.)
stagni: stagnum, -ī (n.) — standing water, pool, lake (gen. sg.)
sterneret: sternō, -ere, strāvī, strātum — to spread out, lay level, smooth (3rd sg. impf. subj., purpose clause)
strepuerunt: strepō, -ere, -uī, -itum — to make a din, resound, blare (3rd pl. perf. = strepuērunt)
stringentem: stringō, -ere, strinxī, strictum — to graze, skim, strip; hug (pres. part., m. acc. sg., agreeing with quem)
struat: struō, -ere, strūxī, strūctum — to build, arrange, plan, contrive (3rd sg. pres. subj., indirect question)
subvectus: subvehō, -ere, -vēxī, -vectum — to carry up, convey upstream (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg.; 'carried up')
summique: summus, -a, -um — highest, topmost (n. gen. sg., with tēcti) + -que 'and'

tacita: tacitus, -a, -um — silent, still, quiet (f. abl. sg., with undā)
thybri: Thybris, -is (m.) — the Tiber, river and river-god of Latium (voc. sg., Thybrī; also dat. sg.)

umbrosa: umbrōsus, -a, -um — shady, full of shadow (f. nom. sg., with harundō)
